name: example (made-up posts, not a real user)
posts:
Here's the thing about cold email: nobody cares about your product.

They care about their own Tuesday.

I rewrote one email last week. Replies went up. Short wins. Always.

Lost a client today. Painful.

Here's the thing: I told them what they wanted to hear instead of what they needed.

Never again. Honest advice or nothing.

Three rules I follow before sending any proposal:

1. Say the price on page one
2. One option, not three
3. A date to decide by

Boring? Yes. It closes deals.

Hot take: your personal brand is just how you treat people when no one is watching.

Here's the thing, posting daily won't fix a bad reputation.

Fix the work first.

Hired our first support person this week. Nervous and excited.

What I learned: write the playbook BEFORE the hire, not after.

Here's the thing: clarity is kindness.
notes: Why I stopped doing free discovery calls. I now send a short questionnaire first. Fewer calls, better clients.
A mistake I made when I raised my prices: I announced it by email and apologised. Never apologise for your price.
What I look for when I hire a freelancer. Clear writing in the first message matters more than the portfolio.
